chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, in the sky there are two angels assigned to the servants. So whoever is humble to Allah, they raise him (in status), and whoever is arrogant, they lower him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of humility and arrogance according to the angels?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical reality of divine monitoring, where two specific angels act as agents of spiritual elevation or descent based on an individual's humility (tawadu') versus arrogance (takabbur). This narration underscores the Shia concept of continuous divine surveillance, linking internal character traits directly to their cosmic consequences, thereby encouraging believers to cultivate modesty as a means of attaining higher spiritual ranks.
